paras: Ledger's security team found a <g>hidden implant</g> inside hardware wallets sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia.
<u>It read the recovery phrase off the screen during setup and sent it out over a mobile network.</u>
On-chain researchers link it to <r>more than $86M</r> in suspected losses. Ledger hasn't confirmed that figure, and asked resellers in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to pull its devices.

items.l: price of Ledger's new Atom device

paras: Days later, Ledger unveiled <g>Atom</g>: an Android touchscreen device with Ledger OS on a secure element.

→ Android apps kept apart from wallet signing
→ Tamper sensors that work even when it's off
→ Physical switch for camera & mic
→ Solana's Seeker app preinstalled
Deliveries start in <r>summer 2027</r>, pending certification, and only through Ledger's own website.
<u>So the device built to stop this attack arrives next year.</u>
Until then, the oldest rule in self-custody still applies: buy hardware only from the official store, and never use a device that arrives with a recovery phrase already set.
